llm.summary: The skill is a real, purpose-aligned Kia vehicle integration, but it asks users to run mutable npm code with vehicle-account credentials and enables persistent access to sensitive vehicle functions.

dimensions.detail: The setup places Kia username and password values directly in .mcp.json or ~/.claude/mcp.json, which are long-lived plaintext config locations and can expose vehicle location and command capability if leaked.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup runs npx -y kiaaccess-mcp without pinning a reviewed version or integrity metadata, so the code executed by the MCP server can change after review and runs with the supplied credentials.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents write modes and confirmation gates, but the example configuration uses KIA_WRITE_MODE=comfort by default, enabling climate and charging commands rather than starting read-only.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact discloses local remember-me token storage that refreshes sessions silently forever and a plaintext token export tool described as a full MFA bypass; kia_forget_session exists, but persistence is high-impact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifact: it provides Kia account login, vehicle status, location, EV charge information, and confirm-gated vehicle commands for the user's own Kia account.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Prefer read-only mode unless you need commands, avoid storing real Kia credentials in project files, pin and review the MCP package version before running it, and treat exported refresh tokens as equivalent to account access because they bypass MFA on that machine.
llm.findings:
[AS2] expected: Credential use is expected for a Kia account integration, but the artifact-backed concern remains because the documented config stores those credentials in plaintext MCP files while the account can expose vehicle data and commands.
[T08] expected: Using an external MCP package is consistent with the documented integration, but the artifact specifically uses unpinned npx -y execution, leaving the reviewed skill dependent on whatever package version npm resolves later.
[T09] unexpected: The artifact needs credentials to authenticate, but directing users to put the account password in persistent project or user config is not a necessary or well-contained secret-handling pattern.
